transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Time: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PDT)
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Kim (Redwood SE), Leo Sanchez (Redwood), Aisha Rahman (CTO, Clymber), Luca Moretti (Platform Engineer), Priya Desai (SRE), Tommy Nguyen (PM)

Summary (auto):
- Reviewed last week's pilot telemetry; discussed anomalies during burst tests; confirmed canary/A-B breakpoints and rollback criteria; agreed on runbook ownership and smoke-test window.
- Action items assigned for batching tweaks, runbook draft, and KPI targets.

Topics: telemetry burn-in, A/B breakpoints, canary thresholds, cutover dry-run, smoke test, RBAC/KMS concerns, fallback routing

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, going to kick us off, agenda is quick telemetry review, confirm canary thresholds and then runbook/dry run planning
00:12 - Aisha (Clymber): thanks maya, we had a weird spike during the 10k token burst on thursday where the 99th jumped, wanted to understand if that was model cold start or infra queueing
00:28 - Jared (Redwood SE): yeah we pulled the traces, there was a KV cache miss pattern and also a short-lived batch formation delay — looks like a mix. i pushed a small patch to batching heuristics last night that should reduce the window, but we should run a burn-in to validate
00:46 - Luca (Clymber): quick q — the patch changes batching thresholds, does that change cost materially? our finance team watches token/second closely
00:58 - Jared (Redwood SE): minor, maybe 3-6% in some tail scenarios but reduces tail latency and retries which might save overall unit cost; i'll share an expected delta in the log bundle
01:15 - Priya (Clymber): also, we saw a couple 5xx from the health checker during peak — not sure if that's the model or the network shim
01:29 - Leo (Redwood): there's a known edge where kube liveness probes can race with GPU driver restarts under heavy mem pressure; our suggested mitigation is shorter probe timeout plus circuit breaker on the proxy side during canary ramp
01:47 - Tommy (Clymber): we need to map who owns the probe change and who runs the smoke during the window, we can't have ops surprises during business hours
02:02 - Maya (Redwood): agreed. proposal: do burn-in in off-peak, keep initial canary at 1% traffic for 30m, then 5% for 1h with telemetry SLO checks at 5, 30, 60 min. rollback if 99th latency exceeds threshold or errors > 0.5%
02:22 - Aisha (Clymber): what's our 99th threshold number? we haven't given teams explicit values yet
02:31 - Maya (Redwood): Luca, do you have target numbers? if not we can propose defaults — e.g. 95th < 300ms, 99th < 750ms for typical queries; longer for >4k tokens but still relative bounds
02:49 - Luca (Clymber): i can pull historical percentiles from our prod logs, will send by monday. default numbers sound reasonable as starting points
03:03 - Jared (Redwood SE): small note: for long-context requests we recommend a separate route with higher memory nodes, that'll affect cost and routing policy. during canary we should keep mixed traffic gated to avoid memory spike surprises
03:21 - Priya (Clymber): ok that makes sense. for A/B we were planning to validate quality differences between base-llama-3-22k-fp16 and the quantized fast variant — do we expect quantized to change latency vs quality tradeoff much in this setup?
03:42 - Jared (Redwood SE): quantized reduces memory and can shave per-token latency, but you might see subtle hallucination differences on rarely used prompts; recommend A/B with held-out eval set and automatic quality regression alert. we can add a simple eval hook to the pipeline during the 5% ramp
03:57 - Aisha (Clymber): is that eval hook something you host or we run? we have privacy concerns for some prompts
04:05 - Maya (Redwood): two modes: redwood-hosted eval (scrubbed) or customer-side eval. for regulated prompts we recommend customer-side; we'll provide the harness and a small docker image to run locally
04:19 - Tommy (Clymber): on security — SSO/SAML and KMS integration are green right? we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM for compliance
04:28 - Leo (Redwood): yes SAML SSO is in place, KMS integration prototype exists — audit log forwarding we can enable to your ELK/Splunk endpoint; i'll attach the doc in the runbook link
04:43 - Aisha (Clymber): good — we will need SOC2-type attestations in the package for procurement but that can be in the post-cutover packet
04:53 - Maya (Redwood): noted. procurement packet and security checklist will be appended to the runbook.
05:00 - Luca (Clymber): back to canary: what metrics are we gating on? latency, errors, cost, correctness? we need an ordered list for the automated decision engine
05:12 - Jared (Redwood SE): prioritized: 1) correctness regressions (from eval hook), 2) error rate > threshold, 3) 99th latency breaches, 4) cost anomalies (sudden token count spike). we'll put numeric thresholds in the runbook.
05:29 - Maya (Redwood): also include service-level fallbacks: route to hosted fallback smaller model if dedicated capacity is saturated, and an emergency slow-path returning cached answers for known prompts
05:45 - Priya (Clymber): how long does rollback take operationally? what's our expected RTO if we trigger canary rollback?
05:53 - Leo (Redwood): rollback is near immediate at the routing layer (<2m) if criteria hit; model spin-down and cache warm is the time-sink — full steady-state back can take 10-20m depending on KV cache warmup. that's why we pick short initial canary windows
06:12 - Aisha (Clymber): noted, we should show ops runbook with exact steps and escalation matrix; please include contact points and phone numbers for the dry-run
06:23 - Maya (Redwood): yeah will do. runbook will have prechecks, smoke tests, escalation, rollback steps, and postmortem template.
06:35 - Tommy (Clymber): on metrics instrumentation, can you confirm telemetry will include per-route token counts, batching histograms, KV-cache hit/miss and outstanding batch queue length?
06:48 - Jared (Redwood SE): yes, we emit all those. small caveat: batching histograms are sampled for high-volume routes — full resolution logs will be available in synthetic tests.
07:03 - Luca (Clymber): we need to ensure our APM traces link to the token shards, otherwise correlating latency to token spikes is rough
07:12 - Leo (Redwood): we can add trace ids to token-level logs, will add to instrumentation checklist.
07:20 - Aisha (Clymber): any concerns about data residency for EU customers? a few of our customers are EU-only and require logs to stay in region
07:28 - Maya (Redwood): for EU residency we can pin region to eu-west-1 with private deployment option; that's part of private offering and will require extra procurement step but doable
07:40 - Priya (Clymber): budget question: if we use dedicated capacity for canary vs hosted bursts, cost delta?
07:48 - Maya (Redwood): dedicated gives predictability, hosted gives elasticity — we can draft cost scenarios in runbook: dedicated baseline + burst buffer vs hosted pay-as-you-go. i'll include rough numbers in the doc.
08:02 - Tommy (Clymber): ok, timeline-wise we want to go to a dry-run next thursday (2026-07-22), does that work?
08:10 - Maya (Redwood): yes proposing 10:00 PDT for a 1h burn-in/smoke. will invite infra ops, dev and product.
08:18 - Aisha (Clymber): can we also reserve a rollback window right after the hour so we don't get surprised by mid-day traffic?
08:25 - Maya (Redwood): yes we'll have a guarded quiet window and ops on-call for the following 2 hours.
08:34 - Luca (Clymber): about A/B — we want to set breakpoints where we push to full traffic if quality delta < 2% on our eval metric and latency within thresholds; otherwise fallback plan triggers
08:46 - Jared (Redwood SE): we'll add an automated A/B analysis job to compute metrics at 5, 30, 60m with a human sign-off gate if quality delta within 1-3% range
08:57 - Priya (Clymber): for monitoring, what dashboards are you sending? will they be prebuilt?
09:04 - Leo (Redwood): yes, we'll provide prebuilt Grafana dashboards for per-route metrics, a Kibana view for logs, and a simple SLO monitor that can post to slack. links in runbook.
09:18 - Maya (Redwood): ok quick run through of next steps: we draft runbook v1, jared runs synthetic burst and shares logs, clymber shares KPIs. dry-run on 7/22. any blockers?
09:33 - Aisha (Clymber): procurement needs SOC2 cert, but that won't block the dry-run, only prod cutover.
09:40 - Maya (Redwood): understood. i'll attach security packet to runbook.
09:47 - Tommy (Clymber): last Q: during canary if we detect content-sensitive prompts, do we route them to a private-only evaluation lane?
09:56 - Jared (Redwood SE): yes, we can mark prompt classes and route sensitive ones to customer-side eval or on-prem lane; the routing rules are simple label checks.
10:08 - Maya (Redwood): great — we are at time. recap — mine and jared's action items, clymber to send KPIs, schedule smoke test 7/22. send invites and runbook link.
10:20 - Meeting ends

Notes / Links: cutover runbook draft (to be attached), telemetry dashboard (provision link), synthetic test logs (will be shared).

Transcript quirks: occasional speaker mislabels; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K V cache" as "K V cash", "SAML" as "sam-el").
